newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal appoints businessman to head Expo 1998.
newsitem.headline: Portugal appoints businessman to head Expo 1998.

text.p: Portugal's Socialist government on Thursday appointed businessman Jose Torres Campos as the chief organiser of the Lisbon Expo 1998 World Fair after the surprise resignation of former EU Commissioner Antonio Cardoso e Cunha.

Cardoso e Cunha quit on Tuesday, saying he could not maintain a climate of "political neutrality" in the project and that he lacked adequate management conditions. He was appointed by the previous Social Democrat government.

Torres Campos, 64, an electrical engineering graduate who now heads state-owned motorway company Brisa-Autoestradas de Portugal, is a former Socialist deputy and a former Under-Secretary of State for Industry and Energy.
He is also a former president of state owned cement firm Cimpor-Cimentos de Portugal.
Presidency Minister Antonio Vitorino told a news conference that Torres Campos had accepted the government's new job offer.

Portuguese media said the government had to appoint a well-qualified successor to Cardoso e Cunha, a former EU Fisheries Commissioner, as soon as possible to restore confidence in the organisation of Expo 1998.
"The government will do all that it can to guarantee national consensus in favour of the project," Vitorino said.

Press reports had said former Banco Totta e Acores president Alipio Dias was set to become the next chief organiser of Expo 1998, but Vitorino declined to say whether the government had tried to recruit him.
The exhibition, which takes as its theme the world's oceans, will have a strong impact on Portugal's economic growth, boosting jobs and the tourism industry, Vitorino said.
